newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil car output seen rising 10 pct next year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil car output seen rising 10 pct next year.

text.p: Brazilian car output is expected to grow 10 percent next year to 1.99 million vehicles, said Brazil's Motor Manufacturers Association (Anfavea).

Domestic sales are expected to grow 6 percent to 1.62 million vehicles while imports are seen rising by 10 percent to 240,000 units in 1997, said Anfavea's president Silvano Valentino at a news conference.
Silvano said preliminary figures showed a production of 1.8 million cars this year, which is in line with Anfavea's estimates.
In a report released Thursday, Anfavea said vehicle output reached 157,201 vehicles in November, up 15.37 percent from the same month last year.
November output, however, dropped 7.48 percent from the 169,917 vehicles assembled in October due to a lower number of working days last month.
Car output in the first 11 months of the year reached 1.68 million vehicles, up 10.51 percent over a year ago, it added.
Brazil's domestic car sales in November rose 10.78 percent from a year earlier to 137,623 from 124,226 vehicles sold, it said.
Sales dropped 2.92 percent compared with October sales of 141,764 cars. In the first 11 months, domestic sales totalled 1.39 million vehicles, up 11.27 percent a year ago.
Brazilian car manufacturers exported 23,279 units last month, against 15,082 in November 1995, up 54.35 percent, it said.
However, exports fell when compared with the 29,421 cars exported in October, it added.
